text:
leo: hi all, new hire here. connected WireGuard but my dev container can't pull from internal registry (registry.internal:5000). docker pull just hangs. I'm tethering my laptop to phone right now — could that be it?

ria: welcome @leo :wave: Tethering can be funky. Does registry.internal resolve for you? Try `nslookup registry.internal` and `curl -v http://registry.internal:5000/v2/_catalog`

leo: nslookup returns 10.50.12.9, curl just stalls, no connection. other public sites are fine.

matt: if DNS resolves but TCP doesn't, common causes are split-tunnel plus mobile carrier blocking private RFC1918 ranges. Our split-tunnel by default routes only corporate subnets; but mobile carriers often drop traffic to RFC1918 or rewrite NAT.

leo: ok. what's the short-term fix? I need to finish a demo build in ~30m.

anya: you can proxy through the jump host with SSH local port forward for Docker. Example: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_redwood -L 127.0.0.1:5000:registry.internal:5000 jump@bastion.redwood.net` then `docker --config ~/.docker-jump pull 127.0.0.1:5000/myimage:latest`. We have a small how-to in the onboarding guide but I can paste a quick snippet.

leo: tried that, docker tried to contact 127.0.0.1:5000 but tls mismatch (registry uses internal cert). Any tips?

anya: two ways: 1) use `--insecure-registry` in the temporary docker daemon config (only for dev) or 2) do a SOCKS proxy and use `docker` with DOCKER_HOST pointing to a remote machine that has access. SOCKS is more work. For quick demo, add registry.internal and its internal cert to your local trust store and forward port as above.

leo: adding cert seemed painless, now pull is working via SSH forward. thanks!

infra-bot: Ticket INF-9011 opened by leo: "new-hire tethering blocks access to internal registry" Assigned: matt ETA: 3h

matt: long-term we prefer not to rely on ad-hoc cert installs. We'll add an onboarding note: if you plan to work from mobile tethering, prefer using the bastion SOCKS or a full-tunnel WireGuard profile.

leo: is full-tunnel profile something I can request?

matt: yes — eng-infra offers a "full-tunnel-onboard" tag for early hires or dev machines. File a ticket with device hostname and reason and we can enable it for 24-72 hours. After inventory/MDM check we can make it permanent.

leo: filed INF-9011 with device name leo-mbp-01.

anya: quick DNS tip: if your phone's carrier modifies DNS, short-term `/etc/hosts` entries pointing registry.internal -> 10.50.12.9 work, but beware they drift if we rotate IPs. Use only for short tasks.

matt: follow-ups: a) eng-infra to add a short onboarding blurb about tethering (matt) b) devex to add the SSH-registry proxy snippet (anya) c) leo to confirm if they want the full-tunnel tag after MDM check.

leo: thanks all — saved my demo. i'll switch to home WiFi later and confirm. :grin:
